title: Your First Paycheck Is $242 Smaller Than You Think. Here's Why
summary: Jordan does the math on his first paycheck ($18 an hour, 80 hours, $1,440), and the deposit says $1,197.69. This video walks through gross vs net pay, every line on a pay stub, what FICA is, how federal withholding and the W-4 work, why a big refund isn't a bonus, and why pre-tax money costs less. The example uses 2026 federal figures for a single filer with one job and no other income, plus a made-up 3% state tax; your own paycheck will differ. Maya and Jordan are fictional composites.
sources: 2026 standard deduction ($16,100 single) and brackets (10% to $12,400, 12% to $50,400): IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32, October 2025: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf
2026 Social Security wage base ($184,500) and FICA rates (6.2% + 1.45%): Social Security Administration 2026 fact sheet, October 2025: https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2026.html
Average refund (~$3,276, cumulative through May 8, 2026): IRS 2026 filing season statistics: https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/filing-season-statistics-for-week-ending-may-8-2026
Tip and overtime deductions (2025 to 2028, with limits): IRS, Working Families Tax Cuts provisions for individuals: https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/working-families-tax-cuts-individuals-and-workers
